definitions.gloss: an abnormal mass of tissue in the body; a tumor
definitions.explanation: The standard medical term for a tumor — an abnormal growth of tissue that can be either benign or malignant. Used in clinical writing, patient explanations, and news reports on health. Not the same as "cancer" — a tumor may or may not be cancerous.

examples.japanese: {腫瘍|しゅよう}が{見|み}つかった。
{検査|けんさ}の{結果|けっか}、{良性|りょうせい}の{腫瘍|しゅよう}だと{分|わ}かった。
examples.english: The tests showed that it was a benign tumor.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}は{腫瘍|しゅよう}を{手術|しゅじゅつ}で{取|と}り{除|のぞ}くことを{勧|すす}めた。
examples.english: The doctor recommended surgically removing the tumor.

examples.japanese: {定期|ていき}{検診|けんしん}で{早期|そうき}に{腫瘍|しゅよう}を{発見|はっけん}することが、{治療|ちりょう}の{成功率|せいこうりつ}を{大幅|おおはば}に{高|たか}める。
examples.english: Detecting tumors early through regular checkups significantly raises the success rate of treatment.

notes:
A medical term of Sino-Japanese origin, composed of {腫|しゅ} (swelling) + {瘍|よう} (sore, ulcer). Used in clinical and informed health-writing contexts. A casual speaker discussing a lump or bump is more likely to use a vaguer word like {しこり} (lump) or {できもの} (growth).

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION — TUMOR VS CANCER:
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}: tumor — an abnormal mass of tissue, which may be harmless or dangerous.
- {良性|りょうせい}{腫瘍|しゅよう}: benign tumor
- {悪性|あくせい}{腫瘍|しゅよう}: malignant tumor (≈ cancer)
- がん / {癌|がん}: cancer — specifically malignant disease. Not every {腫瘍|しゅよう} is がん, but every がん is a {悪性|あくせい}{腫瘍|しゅよう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}ができる: a tumor forms
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}が{見|み}つかる: a tumor is found (passive-feeling)
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}を{発見|はっけん}する: to detect / find a tumor
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}を{摘出|てきしゅつ}する: to surgically excise a tumor
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}を{取|と}り{除|のぞ}く: to remove a tumor
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}マーカー: tumor marker

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {脳腫瘍|のうしゅよう}: brain tumor
- {悪性|あくせい}{腫瘍|しゅよう}: malignant tumor
- {良性|りょうせい}{腫瘍|しゅよう}: benign tumor
- {原発|げんぱつ}{腫瘍|しゅよう}: primary tumor
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}{内科|ないか}: medical oncology department

SIMILAR WORDS:
- しこり: a lump (felt through the skin) — informal and subjective, used before a diagnosis is made.
- できもの: a growth, sore, or skin eruption — vague, includes pimples, cysts, and small tumors.
- {腫|は}れ{物|もの}: swelling; a lump on or under the skin — slightly more formal than できもの.
- がん / {癌|がん}: cancer — a disease category, not a physical object.

REGISTER:
Medical / semi-formal. Appropriate in health articles, doctor-patient conversations, and news. A casual Japanese speaker explaining a non-serious bump would not use {腫瘍|しゅよう} unless they had been told that by a doctor.
